intro.text: AAR CORP. and its subsidiaries are referred to herein collectively as “AAR,” “Company,” “we,” “us,” and “our” unless the context indicates otherwise. AAR was incorporated in 1955 and we are a leading independent provider of solutions to the global aviation aftermarket. We offer a broad line of products and services to commercial and government aerospace customers. We operate globally in over 20 countries through four business segments: Parts Supply, Repair & Engineering, Integrated Solutions and Expeditionary Services. In fiscal 2025, we continued our efforts to optimize our products and services portfolio to position us for continued strong growth as well as to respond to the industry’s increased demand for aftermarket services. Double-digit sales growth in our new parts Distribution activities was a key contributor to improvements in profitability.

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Consolidated sales in fiscal 2026 increased $527.5 million, or 19.0%, over the prior year primarily due to an increase in sales to commercial customers.
The Parts Supply segment accounted for approximately 45% of our sales in fiscal 2026.
The Repair, Engineering, and Software segment accounted for approximately 35% of our sales in fiscal 2026.
The Government Solutions segment accounted for approximately 15% of our sales in fiscal 2026.
The Legacy Commercial Programs segment accounted for approximately 5% of our sales in fiscal 2026.

Sales to global government and defense customers (including sales to branches, agencies, and departments of the U.S. government) were $923.9 million (27.9% of consolidated sales), $804.3 million (28.9% of consolidated sales), and $681.0 million (29.4% of consolidated sales) in fiscal 2026, 2025, and 2024, respectively.
Our sales to commercial customers, including major airlines and related OEM suppliers, were $2,384.1 million (72.1% of consolidated sales) in fiscal 2026.

We market our products and services globally, with approximately 34.3% of our consolidated sales in fiscal 2026 derived from sales to foreign customers (See Note 15 of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements).
The DoW, DoS, other U.S. government agencies and their contractors are our only customers representing 10% or more of total sales in any of the last three fiscal years.

Sales to unaffiliated customers in foreign countries (including sales through foreign sales offices of domestic subsidiaries) were $ 1,135.4 million ( 34.3 % of sales), $ 951.7 million ( 34.2 % of sales), and $ 770.0 million ( 33.2 % of sales) in fiscal 2026, 2025, and 2024, respectively.

Accordingly, in making its assessment of internal control over financial reporting as of May 31, 2026, management excluded the internal control activities of American Distributors Holding Co., LLC, HAECO Americas, Aircraft Reconfig Technologies and Aerostrat Corp. (see Note 2 of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements) which constituted approximately 7.6% of total sales and 11.8% of total assets as of and for the year ended May 31, 2026.
We have ongoing arrangements with OEMs that provide us access to parts, repair manuals, and service bulletins in support of parts manufactured by them.
In certain markets outside of the United States, we rely on foreign sales representatives to assist in the sale of our products and services.
The success and growth of our business depend on our ability to attract, retain, and develop talented and high-performing employees at all levels of our organization.
Our continued success depends on a workforce of skilled talent.
In addition, our business depends on maintaining a sufficient supply of various products to meet our customers’ demands.

If we were to lose a key supplier, or were unable to obtain the same levels of deliveries from these suppliers and were unable to supplement those purchases with products obtained from other suppliers, it could have a material adverse effect on our business.

Additionally, our key suppliers could also increase the pricing of their products, which would negatively affect our operating results if we were not able to pass these price increases through to our customers.
We rely on subcontractors to perform a portion of the services we agree to provide our customers, and our suppliers provide necessary labor, inventory and component parts.
We also rely on third parties to host certain enterprise systems and to manage and host our data and that of our customers.
Our business also depends on using certain intellectual property and tooling that we have the right to use pursuant to license grants under our contracts with OEM customers.
We rely on and may not be able to protect our rights in the unpatented technology, trade secrets, and confidential information we use to conduct our business.

Goodwill is evaluated for impairment either under a qualitative or a quantitative assessment approach, which depends on the facts and circumstances of a reporting unit, consideration of the estimated excess of a reporting unit’s fair value over its carrying amount, and changes in the business environment.

If we determine that it is more likely than not that a reporting unit’s fair value is less than its carrying value, a quantitative goodwill impairment test is performed which relies upon significant judgments and assumptions about expected future cash flows, weighted-average cost of capital, discount rates, expected long-term growth rates, operating margins and on the selection of guideline public companies.

The timing of expenditures depends on a number of factors, including the nature and extent of contamination, the timing of regulatory approvals, the complexity of the investigation and remediation, and the standards for remediation.

Variable lease payments that depend on an index or a rate are included in the determination of ROU assets and lease liabilities using the index or rate at the lease commencement date, whereas variable lease payments that do not depend on an index or rate are recorded as lease expense in the period incurred.
